title: Aishwarya Rai Just Landed in France to Close Cannes 2026. L'Oréal Left Her Off the Poster. She Showed Up Anyway.
excerpt: The actress who put India on the Cannes red carpet in 2002 is back for the closing ceremony — with Aaradhya in tow, a Gucci bag, and 24 years of refusing to be written off.
body:
The posters at Hotel Martinez in Cannes this year featured L'Oréal Paris's ambassador lineup for 2026. Alia Bhatt was there. Aditi Rao Hydari was there. Huma Qureshi was there.

Aishwarya Rai Bachchan — the woman who has represented L'Oréal at Cannes since 2003, who was the first Indian actress to walk the festival's red carpet, who served on its jury — was not.

The internet noticed. It was not polite about it.

And then, on May 22, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan walked through Mumbai airport in a black Dhruv Kapoor blazer, Gucci bag in hand, daughter Aaradhya in a matching all-black outfit beside her, and boarded a flight to the French Riviera. She is expected to attend the closing ceremony of the 79th Cannes Film Festival on May 23.

She didn't issue a statement. She didn't post a defiant caption. She just showed up. That's the move.

## The L'Oréal Controversy, Explained

L'Oréal Paris has been Aishwarya's longest brand relationship — over two decades. She's been the face of the brand at Cannes since before most of its current ambassadors had their first film release. So when the brand's promotional materials at Hotel Martinez featured every Indian ambassador except her, the omission hit differently.

Fans erupted on social media, calling it a disrespect to someone they see as the original queen of Indian representation at Cannes. The hashtag #AishwaryaAtCannes trended across India. Memes comparing the poster to a family photo with the matriarch cropped out went viral.

L'Oréal eventually responded with a vague statement defending Aishwarya's continued association with the brand. But the damage — or at least the narrative — was already set.

## Why This Matters Beyond Red Carpet Drama

For the Indian diaspora, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan at Cannes isn't celebrity gossip. It's cultural memory.

She walked that red carpet for the first time in 2002, alongside Shah Rukh Khan, for the premiere of *Devdas*. She wore a Neeta Lulla saree that became one of the most discussed Indian fashion moments in global entertainment history. In 2003, she became the first Indian actress to serve on the Cannes jury — a distinction no one has matched since.

For NRIs who grew up in the 2000s, Aishwarya at Cannes was one of the few moments when India felt genuinely visible on a global stage that wasn't cricket or IT. Before Priyanka Chopra went to Hollywood, before Deepika Padukone walked for Louis Vuitton, before Alia Bhatt became a red-carpet regular — there was Aishwarya, showing up year after year, making the case that Indian women belonged in those rooms.

The L'Oréal poster incident stung because it felt like erasure of that history. Not by the world, but by the brand she'd helped build.

## Aaradhya and the Generational Shift

The airport photos show something else worth noting: Aaradhya Bachchan, now 14, walking confidently beside her mother in a coordinated black outfit. For a child who's been photographed at Cannes since she was a toddler, this is becoming her own tradition.

Fans have been quick to frame it as a generational passing of the torch — though Aishwarya doesn't seem remotely interested in passing anything. She's still very much holding the torch.

## The Closing Ceremony

Reports from Moneycontrol and multiple Bollywood outlets confirm that Aishwarya is expected to attend the Cannes closing ceremony on May 23. If she walks the red carpet, it will be her 24th year at the festival — a streak that no other Indian celebrity comes close to matching.

The closing ceremony is traditionally the festival's most prestigious event, with the Palme d'Or announcement and a final red carpet. For Aishwarya to choose this moment — after the L'Oréal controversy, after the initial speculation that she might skip the festival entirely — is a statement in itself.

## What NRIs Are Saying

Across Twitter, Instagram, and diaspora WhatsApp groups, the reaction has been overwhelmingly in one direction. "The real queen is about to take over," posted one fan account. "Cannes is Aishwarya's house. She's just letting others rent it," wrote another.

The sentiment isn't just celebrity worship. It's about what Aishwarya represents: a generation of Indian visibility that was earned, not given, and that apparently still needs to be defended.

She'll walk the carpet tomorrow. And whatever she wears, the real statement was already made at Mumbai airport — in a black blazer, with her daughter, heading to a party she was almost written out of.
nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up watching Aishwarya represent India at Cannes since 2002, her return to the closing ceremony — despite being omitted from L'Oréal's promotional campaign — is a generational pride moment. She remains the only Indian actress to have served on the Cannes jury.
author: Diaspora Desk
